about.body: This OS is the free and open-source portfolio of Xavier Champoux, a technical artist based in Montreal. It was built around the idea of representing who he is, including his different expertises and passions, through the visual identity and content of the website. The code is available on GitHub, so feel free to check it out! 👀

frontenddev.description: As much as I respect React, I fell in love with how intuitive it is to work with Vue. This led me to Nuxt and the incredible suite of tools and community powering this framework (looking at you VoidZero and Unjs) which I constantly try explore and experiment with.
frontenddev.label: Frontend Development

gamedev.description: This one's obvious. Gamer since my childhood, this was the best way to combine my passions for games, arts, and programming. I have touched a few game engines along the way, but Unreal Engine really caught my attention and still continues to amaze me.
gamedev.label: Game Development

generalist3d.description: It started as some experiments in Maya and other various 3D software until I ended up falling in love with Blender, especially since the arrival of geometry nodes. My main interests are simulation and sculpting but I also enjoy working on the other aspects of 3D
generalist3d.label: 3D Generalist

programmer.description: Behind almost every one of my skills is programming. I've come accross multiple programming languages overtime, but the Typescript ecosystem is definitely my go to, even for non web related projects. I won't lie though, Rust is kind of winking at me.
programmer.label: Programming

uiuxdesigner.description: I have always been passionate about the aesthetics of websites and applications, which naturally led me to UI/UX design. Combined with my frontend development skills, this is the perfect combo to create programming aware designs that are easy to implement.
uiuxdesigner.label: UI/UX Designer

motives.body: Long time fan of Star Wars and futuristic dystopian settings like Blade Runner and Cyberpunk 2077, I tend to criticize through my works the constant evolution of humans and its technology, how it is becoming an extension of our mind and body.{br}{br}Seeing the current state of our society I truly believe it is the best time to reflect on ourselves and our usage of said tools (looking at you A.I.). As a creator of dreams, I can only imagine a world where we live in harmony and peace, but at what cost?
motives.subtitle: motives
motives.title: fiction at its peak

origins.body: It all started in 2009 when I wanted to become a big blue human after crying of fear before even entering the cinema. At that moment I knew what I wanted to do: Create dreams.{br}{br}Originated from Saint-Hyacinthe, I studied visual arts before moving closer to Montreal in order to pursue my passion in VFX.
origins.subtitle: origins
origins.title: a dreamer was born

(UNLIMITED POWAAHHH!!)

about.title: About
about.note: A little about how I think, what I make and what’s next.

1.title: Somewhere between art & technology.
1.body: That’s where I like to be: moving between the two, learning their languages and building bridges.

2.title: Got problems? Call me.
2.body: I love solving problems. And if I can automate something along the way, even better. Repeating myself is not my favorite hobby.

3.title: Always learning. Usually tinkering.
3.body: Outside of work, I build indie games on my own and follow my curiosity through data, finance, learning and technology. The project list tends to grow faster than it shrinks.

capabilities.frontend: Responsive interfaces, web tools and interactive 3D experiences. Structure, motion and performance, working together.
capabilities.uiux: Clear flows, thoughtful systems and useful details. Aesthetics and organization belong in the same conversation.
capabilities.art: Real-time graphics, procedural work, simulation and optimization. Making art and technology speak the same language.
capabilities.programming: Games, tools and pipelines. Solving problems and automating repetitive work whenever possible.

about.robotics: Industrial robotics and automation are a direction I’d love to explore: another way to bring code, systems and the physical world together.

amb.summary: A tile-layout configurator for commercial flooring.
amb.context: An interactive web experience co-developed at Pixistudio for American Biltrite. Users can arrange flooring tiles, customize their designs, and sign in to save their configurations.
amb.contribution: I worked on the UI/UX design and frontend development: building the Vue interface, supporting mobile devices, and implementing localization.

amie.summary: An interactive artwork that turns outfit colors into abstract environments.
amie.context: Amie generates a real-time 3D environment from a visitor’s visual appearance. A custom C++ video tool identifies the colors of their outfit and their relative prominence, giving each person a different result in Unreal Engine.
amie.contribution: I developed the interactive artwork, combining 3D environments in Unreal Engine with the custom C++ color-analysis tool. The project was presented at my Cégep’s final exhibition.

bromont.summary: A real-time 3D map for exploring Bromont’s ski slopes.
bromont.context: An interactive mountain map co-developed with the Pixistudio team for Bromont. Visitors can manipulate the 3D resort map and find information about its slopes and different areas.
bromont.contribution: I worked on 3D integration, frontend development, and interface design: assembling the interactive map in Sketchfab and creating a responsive Vue interface for desktop and mobile.

cloner.summary: A personal spaceship study in hard-surface modeling.
cloner.context: Cloner is a personal spaceship design created during the pandemic. It was a way to explore new visual directions and refine my 3D practice, from detailed forms to the final composition.
cloner.contribution: I designed, modeled, and rendered the spaceship in Blender, using hard-surface and subdivision modeling and experimenting with composition and lighting.

cyberblade.summary: Three tiers of stylized swords, built as real-time game assets.
cyberblade.context: Cyberblade explores how visual complexity can communicate a hierarchy of power. The sword design evolves through three tiers, with each version developed as an asset for Unreal Engine.
cyberblade.contribution: I designed, modeled, retopologized, and rendered the swords in Blender, then created their textures in Substance Painter for use in Unreal Engine.

ecd.summary: A 3D configurator for customizing restored classic cars.
ecd.context: A 3D configurator co-developed with the Pixistudio team for ECD. Users customize classic cars with different colors and materials. URL-based configurations and a quote summary help carry those choices forward.
ecd.contribution: I worked on UI/UX design and frontend development, including the Vue interface and mobile support. ECD’s team created the 3D models.
ecd.credits: Created with the Pixistudio team. 3D models by ECD’s team.

feltkutur.summary: A 3D configurator for shaping spaces with felt.
feltkutur.context: A 3D configurator co-developed with the Pixistudio team for Feltkutur. Arrange felt products and complementary elements in a custom space, with multiselection, an adaptive properties panel, a tile editor, and PDF generation.
feltkutur.contribution: I worked on UI/UX design and frontend development: the Nuxt interface, Three.js integration, mobile support, and localization.

grownshrink.summary: A puzzle-game prototype built around growing and shrinking.
grownshrink.context: GrowNShrink is a small Unity game prototype. Changing size becomes a way to solve puzzles, providing a playground for testing gameplay ideas.
grownshrink.contribution: I developed the prototype while learning Unity and C#, experimenting with the growing and shrinking mechanic and its puzzle possibilities.

identity.summary: Research and short animations about compelling visual effects.
identity.context: Identity asks what makes a digital visual effect compelling in narrative cinema. The research focuses on three ideas: subtlety, immersion, and cognitive dissonance, illustrated through three short animations.
identity.contribution: I developed the research and created the accompanying animations in Blender and Houdini, using each to explore one of the three themes.

living-typo.summary: A generative experiment in how a visual language might evolve.
living-typo.context: Living Typo explores the relationship between language and generative art. Simple behaviors and rules create an organic language-development process, offering a glimpse of an evolving artificial language.
living-typo.contribution: I programmed the generative experiment. The repository documents more of the thinking and process behind the project.

monologue.summary: A Blender animation inspired by the Tears in the Rain monologue.
monologue.context: Monologue is an animated interpretation of Rutger Hauer’s Tears in the Rain monologue from Blade Runner. The original head design comes from Roman Semenenko’s collection.
monologue.contribution: I created the sculpt, retopology, textures, animation, and final render in Blender, working from the credited head design.

ryker.context: A proof of concept co-developed at Pixistudio to explore a more dynamic approach to 3D configuration. The experience combines dynamic pricing, an animated entry and loading sequence, and detailed configuration logic.
ryker.contribution: I worked on UI/UX design and frontend development: building the Vue interface, integrating the 3D model, and supporting mobile devices.

schluter.summary: An interactive showroom that makes hidden layers visible.
schluter.context: An interactive experience co-developed with the Pixistudio team for Schluter’s showrooms. A real-time bathroom scene compares the company’s products with traditional methods, using high-quality rendering, x-ray visualization, and high-resolution captures.
schluter.contribution: I integrated the 3D models and shaders and created the experience logic and UI/UX in Unreal Engine 4. The work combines level creation, Blueprint programming, and real-time graphics.

tile-map-generator.summary: A procedural generator for tile-based game maps.
tile-map-generator.context: Tile Map Generator creates procedural layouts for tile-based games. The algorithm connects a start and an end position while keeping the number of tiles within a specified range, for dungeon layouts and other environments.
tile-map-generator.contribution: I wrote the generator in JavaScript, keeping the algorithm compact and straightforward to adapt to C++ or C#.

unstable.context: Unstable is a school game project with procedural levels, sound, multiplayer inputs, and high-mobility gameplay inspired by games such as Super Smash Bros.
unstable.contribution: I developed the fighting-game prototype, exploring procedural level creation and responsive multiplayer gameplay.
